kp.ayan.hint: Readers mode casts as the KP Readers do (KP New ayanamsa, mean node, 365¼-day dasa years; verified on their worked charts). Automatic uses PL's Krishnamurti ayanamsa, as PL does on its KP pages; with the Solar Fire / Kala Chakra profile it keeps that profile's Lahiri.
kp.used: This page uses {ayanamsa}, {houses} cusps; the ascendant is the beginning of house 1.
kp.differs: Positions here can differ by a few minutes from the other pages, which use the chart's ayanamsa — as in PL, whose KP printouts always use the Krishnamurti ayanamsa.
kp.chartDesc: KP chart: each sign lists the house cusps that fall in it and the planets, with star lord / sub lord and the house the planet occupies.
kp.chartNote: Each sign lists its cusps (number, degree, star/sub lord) and planets (degree, star/sub lord, -house). Houses run from one cusp to the next, so a planet's house can differ from the Rasi chart.
kp.sigHousesNote: As PL defines them: occupants are the planets in the house; their tenants are the planets placed in the nakshatras of the occupants; the owner is the lord of the sign in which the cusp falls; its tenants are the planets in the owner's nakshatras. Rahu and Ketu own no sign.
kp.levelA: houses occupied by the planet's star lord
kp.levelC: houses whose cusp falls in a sign of the star lord
kp.levelD: houses whose cusp falls in a sign of the planet
kp.ayan.readers: Readers mode (KP New, mean node, 365¼-day years)
kp.fortuna: Fortuna (ascendant + Moon − Sun, B1 p. 129): {pos} — sign of {sign}, star of {star}, sub of {sub}.
kp.rank: Significators of each house, strongest first
kp.rankIntro: Krishnamurti's order (B6 pp. 94–95; B3 p. 418): a planet in the star of an occupant is the strongest, then the occupant, then a planet in the star of the owner, then the owner, then planets conjoined with or aspected by these. A node acts for the planets it represents and comes just before them.
kp.lv1: planets in the stars of the occupants
kp.lv3: planets in the stars of the owner
kp.lv5: planets conjoined with (same sign) or aspected by the above
kp.rankNote: A planet whose star holds no planet is a strong significator itself (B6 p. 95). Ownership is by the cusp's sign only, as in all the Readers' tables. Aspects are Parashari sign aspects (Mars 4/8, Jupiter 5/9, Saturn 3/10), the ones the Readers' examples use.
kp.inNodeStar: in {node}'s star: takes that node's houses
kp.psetsNote: A planet gives the results of its star lord (B2 p. 441; B3 p. 56). A node gives its own house, the houses of its star lord, and the full results of the planets it is conjoined with, aspected by, and of its sign lord (B6 pp. 175, 193, 254); a planet in a node's star takes the node's set. These sets reproduce the tables printed in B6 (Figs. 20, 26, 67).
kp.promiseIntro: For each matter KP looks at one cusp: its sub lord decides. If the sub lord signifies one of the matter's houses the matter is promised; if it signifies only the denial houses (the 12th from each), it is denied; both = promised with obstacles (B4 p. 112; B6 p. 282). Click a matter for details.
kp.promiseNote: * denial group derived by the 12th-from rule where the book prints none. Natal retrogression is ignored (B6 p. 154). Shown as research: the Readers judge a natal matter with the dasa and ruling planets too.
kp.sigOfMatter: Significators of the matter's houses, strongest first:
kp.periodsWarn: These are candidates, not predictions. On the Readers' own 11 marriage examples every wedding fell in such a period, but the strength rank alone barely singled it out. Krishnamurti narrows the list with the ruling planets of the moment of judgement and fixes the day by transit — use the two options below and the Transit days button.
kp.rpOnly: Only periods whose lords are all ruling planets now (KP6-046)
kp.levelsTitle: Krishnamurti's level (1 strongest … 5) at which each lord signifies the matter
kp.noPeriods: No period in this range has all three lords signifying the matter.
kp.periodsCut: Showing the first 200 of {n} periods; narrow the years.
kp.periodsNote: Strength = the sum over the three lords of (6 − level): 15 when all three are level-1 significators. A lord that signifies a good and a bad group gives both, in its own periods (B4 p. 184).
kp.levelOf: Level of each planet for this matter:
kp.rp.day: Lord of the day (sunrise to sunrise)
kp.rp.lagnaSub: Sub lord of the rising degree (finer)
kp.rp.rejected: Rejected (in the star or sub of a retrograde planet):
kp.rp.retro: Retrograde ruling planets give results only after they turn direct:
kp.rpNote: Rules: B6 pp. 132–152, 194, 254, 285; B1 pp. 85–95; B5 p. 227. The lord of the rising sign is strongest, then the Moon's star lord, sign lord and the day lord; a node acting for the lagna lord outranks it. Where the lagna's star lord stands is not stated in the Readers; it is put after the lagna lord. Checked on 15 judgement moments printed in the books.
kp.rectIntro: Ask the question, take the ruling planets of that moment (above), and search around the given birth time for the moments whose rising degree has its sign, star, sub and sub-sub lords all among them (B6 pp. 146–152). The Readers then choose by day or night and take the middle of the sub-sub. Reproduces both of B6's worked cases.
kp.rect.rps: Ruling planets used (those in a retrograde planet's star left out, B6 p. 147):
kp.rect.none: No moment in the window has all these lords among the ruling planets.
kp.rectNote: Times in the birth chart's zone ({zone} h). Traditional methods (Vighati, the prenatal epoch) are not used: Krishnamurti shows they give many answers (B6 pp. 149–150; B3 pp. 511–515).
kp.tr.intro: The event comes when the transiting body is in a sign, star and sub all ruled by the period lords (and any planets added). Years: Jupiter; months: the Sun; days: the Moon (B5 pp. 226–229; B6 pp. 254, 334).
kp.tr.none: The body does not pass through such a zone in this period.
kp.tr.cut: Searched the first {days} days of the period.
kp.tr.note: Checked on five dated predictions in B6; two of the book's dates are 2–3 days off the zone (named in the tests).
kp.horIntro: The querist names a number from 1 to 249. Its sign–star–sub unit gives the ascendant; the other cusps are found for that ascendant at the latitude of judgement; the planets, ruling planets and dasa are those of the moment and place of judgement (B6 pp. 108–113). Checked on B6's 37 printed horary charts.
kp.hor.question: Question
kp.hor.retroWait: retrograde: delay until it turns direct
kp.hor.dasaNow: Dasa running at judgement (from the Moon of the moment):
kp.hor.when: When: periods of significators that are also ruling planets (next five years)
kp.hor.noWhen: No period in the next five years has all three lords among both the significators and the ruling planets.
kp.hor.relaxed: No period has all three lords among the ruling planets; shown instead: periods whose bhukti and anthra lords are ruling planets (the dasa lord not required).
kp.hor.whenNote: The Readers then fix the day by the Sun's (or Moon's) transit through the sign, star and sub of these lords — see Transit timing (B6 KP6-062).
kp.hor.chartNote: The ruling planets use the degree actually rising at the moment, not the numbered ascendant (B6 p. 212).
kp.guideIntro: {n} of the Readers' {total} chart rules hold for this chart. Each is in our own words with its book and page; the reason in brackets is the condition that fired.
kp.guideNone: None of the chart rules holds.
kp.guideNote: Left out on purpose, as on the NTP page: death, longevity, accidents, danger and disease prognosis. Rules the Readers quote from tradition only to reject are marked as tradition.
ntp.intro: What H. R. Seshadri Iyer's New Techniques of Prediction (NTP) says about this chart: only the rules whose conditions this chart meets are listed, each with its volume and source-page citation. Iyer's rules are guidance for the astrologer; they have not been tested against outcomes here.
ntp.trioNote: Iyer groups the nine planets into three sets of three that share common friendship. When one planet of a set is the Yogi, the other two take on yoga character as well — specially noticed with Rahu, who becomes yoga-like when the Sun or Mercury is the Yogi. Each planet has one enemy, which becomes the Avayogi when that planet is the Yogi (NTP-2 p. 6).
ntp.bhuktiNote: Iyer reads a Dasha from the birth chart, and a Bhukti from both the birth chart and the Dasha chart. In the Dasha chart each Bhukti lord "crosses" a Starter (the beginning of the Bhukti) and a Ruler (its end); the Ruler decides the final result (NTP-2 pp. 22, 34). Click a row's rules to see why. On the planet cards, "Positive side" and "Negative side" mark rules that apply to a planet with both kinds of lordship (Iyer reads each separately, NTP-2 p. 20).
ntp.areasNote: Iyer reads a Dasha area by area: the Dasha lord's house from the Lagna of each division chart decides that area of life — houses 3, 6, 8 and 12 are always bad for it, the 2nd is neutral, the rest good; the division chart outweighs the birth chart (NTP-2 pp. 57–63, 82). The charts are built Iyer's way (his D-11, D-16, D-30 and D-45 differ from Parashara's Light; see the Vargas page for PL's). His death and widowhood readings are deliberately not shown.
ntp.how: Houses are Sripati bhavas: a bhava's lord is the lord of the sign holding its middle, and a planet's bhava is the span it lies in (NTP-1 pp. 93–97). Yoga point = Sun + Moon + 93°20′; Zero Rasis come from the birth tithi. Positive bhavas are 1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 9, 10 and 11, negative ones 3, 6, 8 and 12; a positive sign is the planet's own sign, a negative one a Zero Rasi or its debilitation sign. Combust counts as Iyer's "eclipsed"; Iyer gives no combustion orbs (he took it from the panchanga), so the app's standard orbs are used. The Dasha chart uses the birth week day {weekday} (1 = Sunday), taken from sunrise to sunrise; Iyer does not say which convention he used. Iyer's own worked example (NTP-2 Chart 1) is reproduced exactly by the app's tests.
exp.intro: Experimental: planet states, lordships, yogas and aspects in the Rasi and every divisional chart, laid out for reading at a glance. Each rule is stated where it is used; rules matched to a Parashara’s Light printout say so.
